description: Mobile UI/UX Premium Polish — Cross-platform (iOS + Android) initiative to elevate the mobile experience so it soars above the competition. Focuses on premium visual identity, delightful micro-interactions, contextual haptic feedback, a compelling paid-tier feel, animated navigation, hero parallax, conversational trip planning, map overhaul, and accessibility. Builds on the completed Mobile Security & Auth Hardening and Android App Audit PRDs.

userStories.title: Add biometric authentication (Fingerprint / Face) to Android

Handle all BiometricPrompt error codes gracefully (ERROR_HW_UNAVAILABLE, ERROR_NO_BIOMETRICS, ERROR_LOCKOUT, etc.)
Clear biometric preference on sign out
userStories.notes: FIXED: Created BiometricAuthService.kt with Class 3 (strong) biometric support via AndroidX Biometric library. Uses BiometricPrompt with suspend/resume for coroutine integration. Preference stored securely in EncryptedSharedPreferences via SecureStorage. Biometric lock screen on app launch with retry. All BiometricPrompt error codes handled (ERROR_HW_UNAVAILABLE, ERROR_NO_BIOMETRICS, ERROR_LOCKOUT, ERROR_LOCKOUT_PERMANENT, ERROR_TIMEOUT, etc.). Biometric preference cleared on sign out via AuthViewModel. MainActivity extended to FragmentActivity for BiometricPrompt compatibility.

userStories.title: Add certificate pinning for Supabase API calls on Android

userStories.notes: FIXED: Created CertificatePinningService.kt with OkHttp CertificatePinner using same SPKI SHA-256 hashes as iOS (Let's Encrypt R3, ISRG Root X1, DigiCert Global Root G2). Integrated into SupabaseClientProvider via Ktor OkHttp engine. Debug mode uses report-only (logs but allows), production mode blocks mismatches. Pins *.supabase.co domain.

userStories.notes: FIXED: Created RootDetector.kt matching iOS JailbreakDetector.swift with 5 checks: su binary paths, root management apps (Magisk, SuperSU, Xposed, etc.), suspicious paths, test-keys in Build.TAGS, writable system paths. Skips checks on emulator to avoid false positives. Shows non-blocking AlertDialog warning on app launch. Integrated into MainActivity with dismissible warning.

userStories.title: [CRITICAL/SECURITY] Sign-out leaks user data — clear all caches, Keychain, favorites, search history, session-timeout state
userStories.description: AuthService.signOut() (Services/AuthService.swift:108-118) only clears in-memory auth state and resets the biometric preference. It does NOT call QueryCache.shared.clearAll(), KeychainService.shared.deleteAll(), FavoritesService reset, SearchHistoryService.clearAll(), SpotlightService deletion, or SessionTimeoutService.stopTracking(). After sign-out a second user on the same device can see the previous user's cached profile, favorites, recent searches, and Spotlight-indexed content. Also leaves stale session-timeout timestamps in the Keychain.
acceptanceCriteria: AuthService.signOut() calls QueryCache.shared.clearAll() to wipe disk cache
AuthService.signOut() calls KeychainService.shared.deleteAll() (after biometric reset reads its key)
AuthService.signOut() resets FavoritesService (favorite ids cleared in-memory and persisted state purged)
AuthService.signOut() calls SearchHistoryService.shared.clearAll()
AuthService.signOut() calls SpotlightService deletion to remove indexed favorites from system search
AuthService.signOut() calls SessionTimeoutService.shared.stopTracking()
Cleanup runs even when supabase.signOut() throws (use defer / do-finally semantics)
Repeat sign-in on same device shows empty Favorites/Search History until user re-loads
userStories.notes: FIXED (commit c258154): AuthService.signOut() now wraps cleanup in a defer block that fires even if supabase.auth.signOut() throws. Order: reset in-memory auth state → BiometricAuthService.reset() (reads its Keychain entry before it's wiped) → SessionTimeoutService.stopTracking() → SearchHistoryService.clearAll() → FavoritesService.reset() → Task.detached { SpotlightService.removeAllItems(); QueryCache.clearAll() } → KeychainService.deleteAll(). FavoritesService.reset() zeroes favoriteEventIds/favoriteRestaurantIds/favoriteAttractionIds and removes the local UserDefaults fallback keys. Verified: sign out on flaky network still purges local data; next sign-in on the same device shows empty Saved/Search History.

userStories.title: [CRITICAL/SECURITY] Session timeout never signs the user out
userStories.description: SessionTimeoutService.checkTimeouts() (Services/SessionTimeoutService.swift:119-161) sets sessionState = .expired when idle/absolute thresholds are reached, but no observer in App or AuthService calls AuthService.signOut(). The user remains authenticated indefinitely; .expired is purely informational. This violates the documented 'Auto-sign out when timeout is reached' acceptance criterion in AND-SEC-005 / IOS session security stories.
acceptanceCriteria: DesMoinesInsiderApp observes SessionTimeoutService.sessionState and triggers signOut() on .expired
On expiry, user is returned to AuthView with a one-time toast/alert: 'Signed out for inactivity.'
Warning state surfaces a non-blocking banner with minutesRemaining and a 'Stay signed in' button that calls recordActivity()
Tracking starts after successful sign-in (in AuthService.startAuthListener .signedIn branch) and stops on .signedOut
isSessionValid() is consulted on cold-launch and triggers signOut() before MainTabView renders if false
Tested: leave the app open for >idle threshold (mocked to 30s in DEBUG) and confirm AuthView re-appears
userStories.notes: FIXED (commit c258154): AuthService.startAuthListener now calls SessionTimeoutService.startTracking(isAdmin:) on .initialSession/.signedIn/.tokenRefreshed and stopTracking() on .signedOut. SessionState made Equatable so DesMoinesInsiderApp can .onChange(of:); on .expired we sign out and show a 'Signed out for inactivity' alert. Cold-launch calls sessionTimeout.isSessionValid() and signs out before authenticated UI renders. A new SessionTimeoutBanner surfaces the .warning state with minutesRemaining and a 'Stay signed in' button that calls recordActivity().

userStories.title: [HIGH/SECURITY] Biometric lock screen has a 'Skip' button that bypasses authentication
userStories.description: DesMoinesInsiderApp.swift BiometricLockView (lines 179-183) renders a 'Skip' button that calls onUnlock() directly, defeating the purpose of biometric protection. A device thief can bypass Face ID/Touch ID with a single tap. Skip is also offered before the user has had a chance to retry, and there is no fallback to email/password re-authentication.
acceptanceCriteria: Remove the 'Skip' button entirely from BiometricLockView
Replace with a 'Sign Out' fallback that calls AuthService.signOut() and routes back to AuthView
BiometricLockView automatically invokes biometric.authenticate() on first appear (no extra tap)
After 3 failed attempts, force the Sign Out fallback (no infinite retry)
Lock screen blocks all underlying app content (full-screen ZStack already does this — verify no leakage)
VoiceOver: Sign Out button has accessibilityLabel 'Sign out and use password to re-authenticate'
userStories.notes: FIXED (commit c258154): BiometricLockView rewritten — Skip button removed, replaced with a destructive 'Sign Out' button (accessibilityLabel 'Sign out and use password to re-authenticate') that calls AuthService.signOut() and lets the app shell route back to AuthView automatically. View auto-invokes biometric.authenticate() in .task on first appear; subsequent retries go through the 'Try Again' button. After 3 failed attempts the retry button is disabled (grayed) and the prompt explains to sign out. Removed the duplicate authenticate() call from the parent DesMoinesInsiderApp .task so we never fire two simultaneous evaluatePolicy calls.

userStories.title: [MEDIUM/PERFORMANCE] Map annotations recompute on every read; no clustering

acceptanceCriteria: Convert annotation arrays to @Published stored properties recomputed only when source data changes

Tapping a cluster animates the camera to ~2.5× closer zoom so members separate out. New ClusterMapPin view renders the count with size/opacity scaling and category tint.

userStories.title: [MEDIUM/PERFORMANCE] Restaurant client-side filtering blocks main thread
userStories.description: RestaurantsViewModel.swift:183 runs .filter { $0.isOpenNow() } and string-matching across 100+ restaurants on the main thread on every filter toggle. Causes UI jank, especially on older devices.
acceptanceCriteria: applyClientFilters() / applyClientSide() dispatched to a background queue (Task.detached)
Filter toggle UI is debounced to 150ms (matches existing search debounce at line 262)
Filtered results assigned back on @MainActor
No regression in filter responsiveness — user-perceivable latency under 100ms
userStories.notes: FIXED: RestaurantsViewModel.applyClientSide(to:openNow:dietary:) converted to a nonisolated private static pure function, wrapped by a new applyClientSideOffMain(list:openNow:dietary:) that runs the filter inside Task.detached(priority: .userInitiated) and hops the result back to @MainActor on return. fetchRestaurants now awaits the off-main variant after loading. A new scheduleClientFilters() fires a 150ms-debounced Task that cancels its predecessor, so rapid Open Now / dietary toggles coalesce into a single off-main filter pass. Hot no-op path (openNow=false, dietary empty) stays synchronous to avoid the actor hop.

userStories.title: [MEDIUM/PERFORMANCE] Favorites fetched as a single unbounded .in() query
userStories.description: FavoritesService.swift:113-125 / 222-234 fetches every favorite event/restaurant in a single .in('id', values: ...) query with no pagination. Power users with 100+ favorites pay the full decode cost on every Favorites tab open.

Cache decoded favorites in QueryCache with a short TTL (5 min)
Background prefetch of next page when within 5 cells of the end

userStories.notes: FIXED: FavoritesService exposes fetchFavoriteEventsPage / fetchFavoriteRestaurantsPage / fetchFavoriteAttractionsPage — each returns a FavoritesPage<T> with items + hasMore. Slicing is deterministic via the sorted() favorite-ID set so pages are stable across loads. Default page size is FavoritesService.favoritesPageSize (25). The legacy fetchFavoriteEvents / fetchFavoriteRestaurants / fetchFavoriteAttractions are now thin convenience wrappers that walk pages internally. FavoritesViewModel was rewritten to drive per-section pagination (events / restaurants / attractions) with isLoadingMore* flags, hasMore* flags, and per-row loadMore*IfNeeded(currentItem:) helpers that only fire when the user scrolls within 5 cells of the end. FavoritesView wires .task { await viewModel.loadMoreEventsIfNeeded(currentItem: event) } on every event/restaurant/attraction row and renders a ProgressView spinner at the tail of each section while the next page is fetching. Tab open with 100+ favorites now renders the first 25 immediately instead of decoding everything up-front.

userStories.title: [LOW/SECURITY] Keychain accessibility flag could be tightened
userStories.description: KeychainService.swift:27 uses kSecAttrAccessibleAfterFirstUnlockThisDeviceOnly so tokens are accessible while the device is locked (after first unlock since boot). For an app that does not run background tasks requiring Keychain reads while locked, kSecAttrAccessibleWhenUnlockedThisDeviceOnly is stricter and reduces the post-compromise window.
acceptanceCriteria: Audit which background tasks (push notification handlers, BGTaskScheduler) read Keychain values
If none require locked access, switch to kSecAttrAccessibleWhenUnlockedThisDeviceOnly
Migration path: read existing items under old flag, re-save under new flag on first launch after upgrade
No regression in cold-launch UX (biometric prompt order remains unchanged)
userStories.notes: FIXED: KeychainService.save() now uses kSecAttrAccessibleWhenUnlockedThisDeviceOnly (exposed as static let accessibility so future changes stay centralised). Audited all Keychain consumers — AuthService, SessionTimeoutService, BiometricAuthService, SettingsView — none require locked access; PushNotificationService does not read Keychain. Added migrateAccessibilityIfNeeded() that enumerates every generic-password item under the service bundle, reads each account+data, and re-saves via delete()+save() so existing installs get re-stamped with the stricter flag. Gated by a UserDefaults migration version (keychain.accessibilityMigrationVersion = 1) so it only runs once per upgrade. Called from DesMoinesInsiderApp.task before QueryCache.pruneExpired so later Keychain reads land on the new flag. Biometric prompt ordering unchanged.
